results.notes:
The bus, the cancel fan-out and the /readyz report are built with every new switch off. With MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_CONTROL_BUS off, attach does nothing, cancel falls through to the old 404, and /readyz still answers plain "ok". The tests the plan names for this slice pass. No partial edits from an earlier attempt were found.

Behaviour added:
- run_control.rs:
  - `attach(cancels, request_id, run_id)` subscribes to `mp.v1.runctl.req.{id}.*` and, when the stream has a run, `mp.v1.runctl.run.{run_id}.cancel`. It is bounded to 250 ms and best effort, and the listener is held in the cancel-registry entry, so `finish` drops it.
  - `cancel_stream` and `cancel_run` return `CancelRoute` (Local, Peer, NoOwner or Unavailable). The local registry wins; the bus is asked only on a local miss.
  - The owner handler honours only Cancel ops for its own request or run id. Queue and probe get "not here" until S3.
  - The run-keyed cancel subject has no loop observer; WS03-S3 plugs that in later.
  - A NATS `listen` cancelled half way now aborts its serving tasks, which the attach budget needs.
  - `LoopbackHub::listener_count()` and `RunControl::degraded()` (pub(crate)) were added for tests.
- cancel_registry.rs: each entry holds an `Option<RemoteListener>`, set by `attach_remote`.
- sse.rs: one call-in after `register_run`, before the spawned task that emits `connected`. A ZDR turn returns into its direct stream before this point, so it never attaches.
- http_routes.rs:
  - `invoke_cancel` answers 202 as before for a local hit and 202 with `via:"peer"` for a peer. A missing or foreign stream is the unchanged 404. An owner that times out or fails is 503 `{error:"run_control_unavailable", retryable:true}`.
  - ZDR callers' Stop stays local and puts nothing on the bus.
  - `cancel_run` also asks the run subject on a local miss. Its response is unchanged and its log line gains `via` (local, peer, unavailable or none).
  - `/readyz` reports the bus state. 200 is kept while degraded.
- Tests: the new two-replica file covers cross-replica cancel, wrong user or org, no owner, a muted owner giving 503, a listener removed on finish, run-cancel fan-out, bus off, `zdr_turn_registers_no_run_control_listener` and a source-order guard on the call-in. Unit tests were added in run_control.rs and cancel_registry.rs. In http_routes.rs I added the peer/via test, a readyz bus-state test, and updated the cancel-log and readyz tests.

results.notes: No partial edits were found from an earlier attempt; all five files are new. chain.go is a pure package (no DB, clock or keys). API: GenesisHash, CanonicalDetails, RowHash (VAC1 as in the plan row), AttestationPayload (VAH1), CheckpointPayload (VAK1), plus the Row type and sentinel errors. Details are canonicalised with UseNumber and number tokens kept verbatim (1.0, 1e3 and 1000 stay distinct), keys sorted by UTF-8 bytes, and an explicit hand-written string escape (not encoding/json) so the bytes cannot move with a Go release. Signed-payload times are UTC with fixed microsecond width. An org id containing a newline is refused in signed payloads. vectors.json was generated by an independent Python reference written from the format description, and the Go code matched it on the first run. The vectors file sha256 (LF) is pinned in a test constant and recorded in the ADR: a4d3e9a8a3beec560015d0d7b6eb5dd1c9312585d4210eb7c8daff14fe7e73cf. The ADR is apps/AUDIT_INTEGRITY_ADR_2026-10-23.md, headed ADR-0013 (placeholder number per DEC-39), with the encoding spec plus the DEC-35 decisions as the plan default, not as ratified. The CI workflow has a test job (Postgres 16, go vet, go test -p 1 with TEST_DATABASE_URL, build of every cmd binary) and a promtool job. The promtool job runs check rules and test rules over apps/Control Plane/observability/rules/*.rules.yml and *.rules.test.yml, and does nothing if none exist. It uses go-version-file go.mod, has no branches filter on pull_request, and adds model-plane to the push branches. No runtime change; no switch added.
